newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Real Software price range due by mid-May.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Real Software price range due by mid-May.

text.p: A price range for shares in Belgian information technology (IT) services firm Real Software, to be listed on the Brussels bourse in early June, will be set at around mid-May, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
The spread between the lower and the higher price would amount to 12 to 13 percent, analysts said.
It was not immediately clear when the final issue price would be announced.

The price range had been expected to have been set on Tuesday, but the company spokesman said watchdog the Bank and Finance Commission, which has to approve the offering, had banned the company from making such an announcement.
Industry sources said first contacts with the BFC had been positive.

Real Software, currently management-owned, is offering about 450,000 existing shares, or 38 percent of its capital, to the public in the deal lead managed by KB Securities and co-lead by Generale Bank and Bank Degroof.
Financial analyst Johan Pede at KB Securities said it was hard to give comparable price/earnings ratios for the sector. "The range is very wide...15 to 40."
For example, New York listed U.S. Electronic Data Systems, active in the same sector, has a current P/E of about 39 based on weak 1996 earnings and an estimated 1997 P/E of 17.
Pede had no comment on Belgian newspaper reports that the operation could be worth 700 million Belgian francs to the company.
Pede said Real Software had known uninterrupted growth in profit and sales since its foundation in 1986.
The software development and implementation company has 400 employees, annual turnover of some 1.2 billion francs, of which one third is realised abroad, and pre-tax profit of 180 million francs.
Pede put operational (Earnings before Interest and Tax, EBIT) margins in the sector at 10 to 20 percent and foresaw market growth of 10 to 20 percent in the 1997-2000 period.
He said the risks for a stock such as Real Software were limited. "The company has preferential partnerships with numerous large companies."

Prospects were good with a view to a need for IT services in the run-up to the year 2000, when changes in dates could cause disruptions to hard- and software and databases, and the launch of Europe's single currency, the euro, he said.

Real Software is the second Belgian IT firm to come to the market in the first half of 1997. Systemat NV, founded in 1984, offers hardware, configuration, assembly, installation, training and support services.
Systemat stock closed down 18 francs at 1,290 on Tuesday on a firmer Brussels bourse.
A study by Vermeulen Raemdonck, the brokerage of bank BBL which lead-managed the issue, put Systemat's estimated 1997 P/E at 14.9 and 11.2 for 1998.
